{{nihongo|'''Iwaya Shrine'''|岩屋神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Harima Province]].

'''Iwaya Shrine''' (いわやじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in Zaimokuchō, {{ill|Akashi, Hyōgo|ar|أكاشي (هيوغو)|arz|اكاشى, هيوجو|az|Akaşi|azb|آکاشی، هیوقو|bg|Акаши|ca|Akashi|ce|Акаси (гӀала)|ceb|Akashi (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Akashi|eo|Akaŝi|es|Akashi (Hyōgo)|et|Akashi|fa|آکاشی، هیوگو|fi|Akashi|fr|Akashi|ga|Akashi|gl|Akashi|id|Akashi, Hyōgo|it|Akashi|ja|明石市|ko|아카시시|lt|Akašis|ms|Akashi, Hyōgo|mzn|آکاشی، هیوگو|nl|Akashi|no|Akashi|pl|Akashi|pt|Akashi|ro|Akashi|ru|Акаси (город)|sh|Akashi, Hjōgo|simple|Akashi, Hyōgo|sr|Акаши|sv|Akashi|tg|Акаши|th|อากาชิ|tl|Akashi, Hyogo|tr|Akashi|tt|Акаси (шәһәр)|uk|Акасі (Хіоґо)|ur|آکاشی, ہیوگو|uz|Akasi|vi|Akashi, Hyōgo|war|Akashi, Hyōgo|zh|明石市|zh_classical|明石市|zh_min_nan|Akasi-chhī|zh_yue|明石|qid=Q26406}}, {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|Q130290|qid=Q130290}}. It is known for its maritime ritual festival called the “Oshataka Festival.” It is one of the {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|ja|論社|qid=Q135022904}} (disputed shrines) identified with '''Iwatsuhime Shrine''' listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} for {{ill|Harima Province|be|Харыма (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Harima|ceb|Harima (baranggay sa Hapon)|cs|Provincie Harima|de|Provinz Harima|es|Provincia de Harima|fa|ولایت هاریما|fr|Province de Harima|gl|Provincia de Harima|id|Provinsi Harima|it|Harima (provincia)|ja|播磨国|ko|하리마국|lt|Harimos žemė|nl|Harima (provincie)|pt|Província de Harima|ru|Харима (провинция)|simple|Harima Province|sk|Harima (provincia)|sr|Провинција Харима|tr|Harima (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Харіма|zh|播磨國|zh_min_nan|Harima-kok|qid=Q1047523}}, {{ill|Akashi District, Hyōgo|Q11512561|qid=Q11512561}}.

=== Enshrined Deities ===
The principal deity is {{ill|Izanagi|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q813858}}, with {{ill|Izanami|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto|qid=Q682306}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōhirume-no-Mikoto}} (Amaterasu), {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ar|تسوكويومي|az|Tsukuyomi|bcl|Tsukuyomi|ca|Tsukuyomi|cs|Cukujomi|da|Tsuki-yomi|de|Tsukuyomi|el|Τσουκουγιόμι|eo|Cukujomi|es|Tsukuyomi|eu|Tsukuyomi|fa|تسوکویومی|fi|Tsukuyomi|fr|Tsukuyomi|hr|Tsukuyomi|hu|Cukujomi|hy|Ցուկույոմի-նո-Միկոտո|id|Tsukuyomi|it|Tsukuyomi|ja|ツクヨミ|ko|츠쿠요미|mk|Цукујоми|mni|ꯁꯨꯀꯨꯌꯣꯃꯤ-ꯅꯣ-ꯃꯤꯀꯣꯇꯣ|no|Tsukuyomi|pl|Tsukuyomi|pt|Tsukuyomi|rsk|Цукуйоми|ru|Цукиёми|sh|Tsukuyomi|simple|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|sl|Cukijomi|sr|Цукујоми|su|Tsukuyomi|sv|Tsukuyomi|ta|சுக்குயோமி|th|สึกูโยมิ|tr|Tsukuyomi no Mikoto|uk|Цукуйомі|vi|Tsukuyomi|zh|月讀|zh_min_nan|Tukuyomi|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hiruko-no-Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993}} enshrined as associated deities.

The shrine is said to bestow blessings of household safety, prosperous business, good fortune, protection from calamity, and matchmaking.

=== History ===
According to shrine tradition, on June 15 in the 13th year of {{ill|Emperor Seimu|Q316672|qid=Q316672}}, the shrine was founded by imperial command by transferring ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=kanjō}}) the deity from Iwaya on {{ill|Awaji Island|ar|أواجي (جزيرة)|az|Avaci adası|bcl|Isla nin Awaji|be|Авадзі (востраў)|bg|Аваджи (остров)|bn|আয়াজি দ্বীপ|ca|Illa d'Awaji|ceb|Awaji Shima|cs|Awadži|da|Avaji|de|Awaji-shima|el|Αβάτζι|eo|Aŭaĝi|es|Isla Awaji|et|Awaji saar|eu|Awaji uhartea|fa|جزیره آواجی|fi|Awaji|fr|Awaji-shima|gl|Illa de Awaji|he|אוואג'י (אי)|hi|अवाजी द्वीप|hy|Ավաձի (կղզի)|id|Pulau Awaji|it|Isola Awaji|ja|淡路島|ko|아와지섬|la|Insula Awaji|lb|Awaji-shima|lt|Avadžis|nl|Awaji (eiland)|pl|Awaji (wyspa)|pt|Ilha Awaji|ro|Insula Awaji|ru|Авадзи (остров)|sl|Avadži (otok)|sv|Awaji|tg|Ҷазираи Авадзӣ|th|เกาะอาวาจิ|tr|Awaji Adası|uk|Авадзі|vi|Awaji (đảo)|wuu|淡路岛|zh|淡路島|qid=Q504373}}<ref name="由緒">{{Cite web |Japanese |url=http://iwayajinjya.com/origin.html |title=Iwaya Shrine – History |access-date=2024-10-08 |publisher=Iwaya Shrine |language=ja |archive-url=  |archive-date=  |url-status= }}</ref>. Another tradition says that in the summer of that same year, a local child became possessed by the deity of Iwaya on Awaji Island, who gave an oracle instructing that the deity be invited to this location, leading to its enshrinement.

The Awaji regional gazetteer *Awaji-gusa*, written in the 8th year of {{ill|Bunsei|de|Bunsei|es|Bunsei|fa|بونسی (دوره)|fr|Ère Bunsei|ia|Bunsei|ja|文政|ko|분세이|ru|Бунсэй|simple|Bunsei|sr|Бунсеи|sv|Bunsei|tr|Bunsei|zh|文政|qid=Q1327119}} ({{ill|1825|Q6997|qid=Q6997}}) by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Watanabe Yōshin}}, records that a {{ill|Bunrei|Q195793|qid=Q195793}} (divided spirit) of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ishiya Shrine}} on Awaji was transferred to Iwaya Shrine in Akashi. When the village heads of Akashiura, known as the Maehama Six, prepared a new boat to transport the deity from Awaji, the sea became extremely rough, preventing them from landing at the beach of Akashiura. Instead, they landed at Akaishi off the coast of Hayashizaki to the west (the origin of the name “Akashi”), where they prayed for protection from maritime disasters and for abundant catches. By dawn the sea had calmed, and they were able to safely welcome the deity to the present site. It is also said that local residents swam out offshore to greet the boat and, deeming it irreverent to ride aboard with the sacred object, pushed the boat while swimming until it reached Iwaya.

Since its founding, the shrine—alongside {{ill|Inazume Shrine|Q11596731|qid=Q11596731}} and {{ill|Watatsumi Shrine (Kobe)|Q11559098|qid=Q11559098|lt=Watatsumi Shrine}}—was revered as one of the great ancient shrines of the Eastern Harima region. It was especially venerated as the tutelary shrine of {{ill|Akashi Castle|Q1151831|qid=Q1151831}}, and was one of the shrines visited annually by the domain lord himself. In the 2nd year of {{ill|Genbun|Q1145754|qid=Q1145754}} ({{ill|1737|Q6993|qid=Q6993}}), the heir of the domain lord {{ill|Matsudaira Naotsune|Q11530528|qid=Q11530528}}, {{ill|Matsudaira Naosumi|Q11530545|qid=Q11530545|lt=Naosumi}}, visited the shrine during the “Armor-Beginning Ceremony,” after which it became customary for heirs to visit the shrine for this rite<ref name="由緒" />.

In the 12th year of {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} ({{ill|1879|Q7783|qid=Q7783}}), the shrine was ranked as a {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=prefectural shrine|qid=Q90139226}}. === Oshataka Boat ===
Every year on the third Sunday of July, the '''Oshataka Boat Ritual''' is held, commemorating the legend of inviting the deity from Ishiya Shrine on Awaji Island<ref>{{Cite web |Japanese|url=http://iwayajinjya.com/osyataka.html |title=Oshataka Boat Ritual |access-date=2024-10-08 |publisher=Iwaya Shrine |language=ja |archive-url= |archive-date= |url-status= }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |Japanese |url=https://akashitowns.com/event/18289/ |title=Akashi’s oldest maritime ritual “Oshataka Boat Ritual” at Iwaya Shrine (Zaimokuchō, Akashi City) |access-date=2024-10-08 |publisher=Akashi Towns |language=ja |archive-url= |archive-date= |url-status= }}</ref>. “Oshataka” is a dialectal corruption of the Akashi phrase *ojatta kanaa*, meaning “Has the god arrived?”<ref>{{Cite web |Japanese |url=https://www.city.akashi.lg.jp/seisaku/kouhou_ka/shise/koho/oshirase/h24/documents/5.pdf |title=Akashi’s ‘Treasures’ Discovery Project: Oshataka—Prayers for Maritime Safety and Abundant Catches |access-date=2024-10-08 |publisher=Akashi City |language=ja |archive-url= |archive-date= |url-status= }}</ref>.

During the festival, young men from the {{ill|Ujiko|Q125562175|qid=Q125562175}} (parishioners), carrying six enshrined deities and nine attendant oshataka boats (each about 2 {{ill|Metre|Q11573|qid=Q11573}} long), stand upright in the water and raise the boats high above their heads while chanting “Oshatakā,” advancing forward in a ceremonial procession. The festival prays for protection from maritime disasters and for bountiful harvests from the sea. In {{ill|1975|Q2479|qid=Q2479}}, it was designated an {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Intangible Folk Cultural Property}} of Akashi City.
